name: Fault improvement by repetition
summary: Two noisy X-X connections in parallel are fault-equivalent to one connection with improved weights.
description: Under *weighted* edge-flip noise, where each edge has weights $(w_X, w_Y, w_Z)$ for its three flips, a square of four X-spiders whose two vertical edges have weights $v = (v_X, v_Y, v_Z)$ and $w = (w_X, w_Y, w_Z)$ (and the other edges weight 1) is fault-equivalent to two X-spiders connected by a single edge with weights $(w'_X, w'_Y, w'_Z) = (\min(v_Z, w_Z), \min(v_Y + w_Z, v_Z + w_Y), \min(v_Z + w_Z, v_Y + w_Y))$, as written in the paper, where the weights on the right are capped at $w'_Y, w'_Z \leq 2$ and $w'_X \leq 1$. Repeating a noisy distribution edge (e.g. a Bell pair between two modules) in this way protects it against the errors that flip the corresponding measurement outcome; iterating gives a ladder of $d$ rungs with weights $(1/\varepsilon, d/\varepsilon, d/\varepsilon)$. As in the paper, noisy edges are labelled with their weight (the cost of a flip on that edge; a vector of weights for the $X$-, $Y$- and $Z$-flips, unlabelled noisy edges have weight 1), and *fault-free* (idealised) edges are drawn bold purple. These annotations are shown on the rule as stated; derived variants (transpose, colour swap, other legs counts) may drop them.
conditions: All weights positive; weighted edge-flip noise.
